title: github.com issue, discussion, wiki and repository pages get a provider signal, so the census decides them without reading
goal: providers.csv carries measured rows (through /kb-probe) for github.com page kinds the census now sends to reading as 'a github.com page (issues, wiki, home) or API call': a wiki page by the wiki's git repository in the bare clone cache, a repository home by its README blob at the default branch, an issue or discussion by the latest timeline time or a hash of its normalized rendered text; census.py check and factdiff.py detect use that signal, so an unchanged page gets bucket OK or factdiff unchanged and a changed one gets review items for its facts; api.github.com stays uncalled. The 2026-09-26 census read 50 such pages, 32 of them confirmed unchanged.

gates.question: What does a repository home's signal hold beyond its README blob at the default branch? A README-only signal would confirm unchanged a repository whose licence, release or archived state changed (the 2026-09-26 reading updated S1976, S2156, S2012 and S1892 for such facts).
options: README blob, licence blob, version-like release tags created since retrieval, and the page's archived banner
gates.recommendation: README blob, licence blob, version-like release tags created since retrieval, and the page's archived banner
gates.answer: README blob, licence blob, version-like release tags created since retrieval, and the page's archived banner

gates.question: How does the provider registry give one host's page kinds (a repository home, a wiki page, an issue, a discussion) their own rows and signals?
options: match takes * for a path segment and a trailing $ for the url's end; one row for each page kind; a new signal name git (a file in a repository of the clone cache) and a version key timeline (the page's latest timestamp)
one row for the host with a per-kind column the fetch tools read
gates.recommendation: match takes * for a path segment and a trailing $ for the url's end; one row for each page kind; a new signal name git (a file in a repository of the clone cache) and a version key timeline (the page's latest timestamp)
gates.answer: match takes * for a path segment and a trailing $ for the url's end; one row for each page kind; a new signal name git (a file in a repository of the clone cache) and a version key timeline (the page's latest timestamp)

gates.question: Which pages does a signal leave out, and how is the retrieval day itself read? A wiki's own git url, a releases list and a pull request have no signal here; activity on the retrieval day is ambiguous because retrieved_utc holds a day.
options: a wiki's own git url is decided by the census check only (its newest commit) and fact diff keeps its path; a releases list and a pull request stay in the reading queue; a commit on the retrieval day is CHANGED and a timeline timestamp on it is OK, as check_ref and check_live already read it
every page kind with a signal is decided by both tools, and the retrieval day is CHANGED for every signal
gates.recommendation: a wiki's own git url is decided by the census check only (its newest commit) and fact diff keeps its path; a releases list and a pull request stay in the reading queue; a commit on the retrieval day is CHANGED and a timeline timestamp on it is OK, as check_ref and check_live already read it

notes: Premise from kb/public/_census/2026-09-26.csv (tally run 2026-10-10): 50 rows of kind gh-page or api-other with note 'github page' went to phase 2: 32 confirmed, 16 updated, 2 superseded. 85 live github.com non-raw sources on 2026-10-10. The signals are measured through /kb-probe before code uses them; a page kind no signal fits stays in the queue. Fact for the no-api rule: census.py's docstring says api.github.com is never called.
